theme_central: A divine debriefing of the battle of Badr: the spoils and the victory belong to Allah; true strength comes from faith and obedience, not numbers.
sources_note: Well-sourced 4-part structure (azlyrahman substack / grokipedia, Ramadan Reading #8): 1-4, 5-18, 19-71, 72-75.

branches.title: The spoils, the true qualities of the believer
branches.resume: A dispute over the sharing of the spoils, immediately reframed: the true prize of victory is the quality of one's faith.

children.t: The spoils belong to Allah and His messenger
Qualities of the true believer: a trembling heart, tawakkul, prayer, charity

branches.title: The divine account of Badr
branches.resume: Initial reluctance of the believers, Allah's promise, direct interventions: sleep, rain, angels.

children.t: Reluctance of the believers before setting out, discussion on how to proceed
Promise of reinforcement by 1,000 angels, the purifying rain
"It was not you who killed them, but Allah" — theological climax

branches.title: Obedience, the plot of the disbelievers
branches.resume: Call to obey Allah and His messenger, the Furqan, the Meccans' plot and their promised defeat.

children.t: Obedience to Allah and the messenger, not betraying trust, the Furqan (discernment)
The disbelievers' plot against the Prophet, their announced defeat

branches.title: Laws of the spoils, firmness, prisoners
branches.resume: Distribution of the spoils (khums), firmness in battle, broken treaties, the status of prisoners of war.

children.t: Distribution of the spoils (khums), firmness required in battle
Treaties broken by the enemy, deterrent military preparation
Encouragement to fight, status and ransom of prisoners of war

branches.title: Closing: principles of the community
branches.resume: Mutual support between emigrants and helpers, timeless principles beyond the event of Badr.

children.t: Alliance and mutual support between emigrants (muhajirun) and helpers (ansar)
